rules.statement: Keep browser-mediated, third-party-cookie-dependent OpenID Connect mechanisms (Front-Channel Logout 1.0, Session Management 1.0) disabled by default: their settings default to false, and a stock provider advertises neither one and sets no browser-state cookie.
rules.why: These mechanisms depend on third-party cookies in iframes, which browsers are removing. The secure default must stay the cookie-independent pair: RP-Initiated Logout and Back-Channel Logout.
rules.check: Look for new or changed defaults for frontchannel_logout_supported, frontchannel_logout_session_supported, session_management_supported or similar settings that become true. Also look for a check_session_iframe or browser-state cookie that is emitted when nothing has enabled it.

rules.statement: Expose an optional protocol capability as an operator-controlled setting that is off by default and drives its discovery advertisement, so enabling it needs only a settings change and no code change or fork.
rules.why: This follows the repository's available-but-off pattern (as with backchannel_logout_supported and code_challenge_methods_supported). It keeps the secure default while letting a deployment that accepts the trade-off turn the capability on.
rules.check: Look for an optional protocol feature that is hard-wired on, enabled through code, or advertised in discovery by a constant instead of by the setting that gates its behavior.

rules.statement: Reject client registration or configuration that uses a capability the provider's discovery settings mark unsupported, such as a frontchannel_logout_uri while frontchannel_logout_supported is false, or frontchannel_logout_session_required while frontchannel_logout_session_supported is false.
rules.why: What the provider does must always match what it advertises.
rules.check: Look for new per-client settings tied to a discovery capability that lack a coherence or validation rule refusing them while the capability is disabled.

rules.statement: When rendering front-channel logout iframes, append the iss and sid query parameters only while frontchannel_logout_session_supported is enabled.
rules.why: The provider must send session parameters only when it advertises that it supports them.
rules.check: Look at the code that builds front-channel logout URIs and confirm it gates iss/sid on the session-supported setting rather than adding them unconditionally.

rules.statement: Treat Front-Channel Logout as a best-effort layer added on top of Back-Channel Logout: enabling it must never disable or bypass back-channel notification.
rules.why: Back-Channel Logout stays the preferred, reliable mechanism. Using the front channel as a replacement is a named smell.
rules.check: Look for logout code paths where enabling front-channel logout skips, replaces or short-circuits back-channel logout_token delivery.

rules.statement: Compute the OpenID Connect session_state as a salted SHA-256 digest over the client id, the origin of the client's redirect URI and the opaque OP browser state, and emit it only while session management is enabled.
rules.why: This is the Session Management 1.0 computation the check_session_iframe script recomputes. The origin comes from the redirect URI so that the relying party's iframe origin matches.
rules.check: Look for a session_state computation that leaves out the salt, uses a different hash or a different origin source, or is stamped on authorization responses while session management is disabled.

rules.statement: Delete the session-management browser-state cookie on logout.
rules.why: The browser-state cookie must change when the session ends so that relying parties polling check_session_iframe detect the change.
rules.check: Look at logout and end-session handlers when session management is enabled and confirm they clear the browser-state cookie.

rules.statement: Allow relying parties to frame only the check_session_iframe page, and let the front-channel logout page frame only the registered clients' logout origins; every other page keeps forbidding framing.
rules.why: Every page the server writes has a strict Content Security Policy and is framed only by design.
rules.check: Look for frame-ancestors or frame-src CSP changes, or X-Frame-Options changes, that allow framing beyond check_session_iframe or allow frame sources other than the clients' front-channel logout origins.

rules.statement: Implement front-channel logout and session management on top of the existing end-user session model and end-session pipeline, without adding persistence, tables or migrations of their own.
rules.why: These mechanisms add no state of their own, so enabling them should be a settings change only.
rules.check: Look for new entities, tables, stores or migrations introduced solely for front-channel logout or session management.
